sections.content: How many people are "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)"?

97,005 people

were counted on the census as "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may provide pastoral care relating to religious denominations, and a variety of welfare-related services including advice on benefits, health, disability and residential care not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)", 12.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" included:

  • electrical and electronic trades (other)
  • routine inspectors and testers
  • process operatives (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" there were more women than men (77.4% compared with 22.6%).

This means "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health and social care associate professionals".

Men made up 22.6% and women made up 77.4% of "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" included:

  • welfare professionals (other)
  • residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors
  • cleaners and domestics

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "welfare and housing associate professionals (other)", 17.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (63.7% compared with 36.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.2%) than self-employed (4.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
